parts:
Moving this post to the shiny-discuss list since it is more of a shiny question than an shinyapps.io question.

On Wed, Mar 9, 2016 at 1:08 PM, Gerson ROMERO RUIZ <gerson....@gmail.com> wrote:
up vote0down votefavorite

I'm trying to make an interactive rMarkdown with a googleVis motion chart in it. The idea is to get a report where I can filter my data and then get a motion chart. So, right now I've got everything working right except that when I run my Document the motion chart is incomplete. Inspecting the html code I found that this is because of the iframe height I know that I can change these direct form the html code but I need a way to change it directly from the Shiny code but I've not been able to find the way. Can anyone please help me?

Here is an example of what I'm trying to do but using the WorldBank dataset:


```{r,echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE}
#Load Packages

    library(shiny)
    library(rmarkdown)
    library(googleVis)
    library(WDI)
    library(dplyr)

    #Get data
    inds <- c('SP.DYN.TFRT.IN','SP.DYN.LE00.IN', 'SP.POP.TOTL',
              'NY.GDP.PCAP.CD', 'SE.ADT.1524.LT.FE.ZS')
    indnams <- c("fertility.rate", "life.expectancy", "population",
                 "GDP.per.capita.Current.USD", "15.to.25.yr.female.literacy")
    wdiData <- WDI(country="all", indicator=inds,
                   start=1960, end=format(Sys.Date(), "%Y"), extra=TRUE)
    colnum <- match(inds, names(wdiData))

    names(wdiData)[colnum] <- indnams
    ## Create a motion chart
    WorldBank <- droplevels(subset(wdiData, !region %in% "Aggregates")) %>% 
      mutate(latlon = paste(latitude,longitude,sep=":"))


    WorldBank <- readRDS("WorldBank_Data.RDS") %>% 
      mutate(region=as.character(region))
    #Filter function
    filter_and_graph <- function(rgn){
      graph_data <- WorldBank %>% 
        filter(region == rgn)

      M <- gvisMotionChart(graph_data,
                         idvar="country", timevar="year",
                         xvar="life.expectancy", yvar="fertility.rate",
                         colorvar="population", sizevar="population",
                         options=list(width=800, height=600))
      return(M)
    }

    #Shiny in markdown
    shinyApp(
      ui = fluidPage(selectInput("rgn", 
                  "Choose your region",
                  choices = unique(WorldBank$region),
                  selected = "Sub-Saharan Africa (all income levels)"),
        htmlOutput("graph")

      ),
      server = function(input, output){
        output$graph <- renderGvis({filter_and_graph(input$rgn)})
      }
    )

```
